You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Yarrow Wharf manifests","question":"Can the dispatcher release the amended loading summary?","claims":{"A":"Container C74 passed its dockside seal integrity check.","B":"The loading crane lifted C74 at 06:25.","C":"C74 is a standard-height container."},"handoff":"The case concerns whether the dispatcher can release the amended loading summary for container C74. The crane lift log (S1) strongly supports that C74 was lifted at 06:25, confirming claim B. The container register (S2) contradicts claim C, showing C74 is a high-cube container, not standard height. Claim A about passing the dockside seal integrity check remains unresolved: while an upstream inspection (S3) noted an intact seal on arrival and a rough lift before the dockside check, it does not explicitly confirm that C74 passed the dockside seal integrity check. This unresolved status on seal integrity is the key issue affecting the decision to release the amended loading summary.","follow_up":{"S4":"the separate dockside seal inspection, after the lift, reports C74's seal passed the integrity check."}}

Claim A was unresolved based on initial evidence but is now supported by the dockside seal inspection report (S4) confirming C74 passed the seal integrity check.
